key_insight: Generative models (including diffusion-based approaches) can achieve high hypervolume yet systematically miss the true Pareto frontier on other MOO metrics; this failure is explained by an "offline-frontier shift" where the dataset frontier and learned frontier diverge.
problem_solved: Diagnoses why state-of-the-art generative methods for offline multi-objective optimization perform poorly on metrics like generational distance and coverage despite strong hypervolume scores, clarifying a systematic distributional limitation.
method: Empirical benchmarking of generative approaches (e.g., diffusion models) against evolutionary baselines across multiple MOO metrics, not just hypervolume.

Introduce and characterize the "offline-frontier shift": the distributional mismatch between the empirical (dataset) Pareto frontier and the true problem frontier that leads generative models to concentrate on dataset-specific frontier modes.
Analytical and experimental linkage between the shift and degraded performance on metrics such as generational distance, coverage and diversity.
impact: Provides practitioners a diagnostic lens to interpret why high hypervolume can be misleading and when to prefer evolutionary or alternative methods; encourages multi-metric evaluation and careful treatment of dataset-induced frontier bias in offline MOO.
visual_elements: Scatter plot: true Pareto frontier vs dataset frontier vs model-generated solutions (color-coded) to show the offline-frontier shift.
Bar chart: comparative performance across metrics (hypervolume, generational distance, coverage) for generative vs evolutionary baselines.
Schematic diagram: concept map explaining offline-frontier shift (dataset frontier → learned frontier → true frontier) with arrows showing directions of bias.
Pipeline comparison: side-by-side flow of a generative MOO method and an evolutionary MOO method highlighting where distributional assumptions differ.
paper_title: The Offline-Frontier Shift: Diagnosing Distributional Limits in Generative Multi-Objective Optimization
paper_authors: Stephanie Holly, Alexandru-Ciprian Zăvoianu, Siegfried Silber, Sepp Hochreiter, Werner Zellinger
